quest.title: A Delicacy for Nara
quest.description: According to Arapacati, the rising pillars of smoke will lead to her brothers who are doing "cooking training." We need to find them and bring them back before the festival starts...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Oh! If it isn't the Golden Nara! Alas...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Arapacati not afraid. Nara {NICKNAME} is good Nara, just like the Nara in the stories. Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon have helped us a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #Okay, Arapacati not afraid. Arapacati trusts Arama, and the grass, leaves, and seeds. All say you're a good Nara. Hello, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, Arapacati!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't make that kind of joke!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: You good. Arapacati knows.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Lots of winds bring lots of small seeds. They come to Vanarana with Nara. They say Nara {NICKNAME} is nice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arama said something like that too! Speaking of which, seeds brought by winds... You mean like dandelion seeds?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is going to help Arana to form a Bija. So, we will prepare for Festival Utsava together.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Oh, Festival Utsava...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Arapacati looks strange. Is anything troubling you?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Arapacati's big brothers have not returned to Vanarana. We siblings can't celebrate Festival Utsava together if they don't return...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I haven't seen Arachatora, Arasaka, Arapas, and Araphala in Vanarana for a very long time either. Never seen them after that incident.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A very long time... How long is that?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Many, many moons ago, when the seedlings had just sprouted. But now they are already big trees, big enough to keep the rain off Aranara! It's seven Arapacatis tall!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From seedlings to trees! Wow! That's a really long time! Are your brothers missing, Arapacati?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Missing? Is that a type of seed?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ooh! So Nara seeds are called Missing? Amazing!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Nara are amazing! Nara {NICKNAME} must have many Missings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that's not what we mean...

choices.text: It means you don't know where they are.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Oh, not like that. Arapacati knows where Arachatora, Arasaka, Arapas, and Araphala are. Brothers not missing.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: They have been training at Vanarana for a long, long time. Cooking training.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, cooking training. Paimon gets it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like something Paimon would be interested in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm! Paimon is more interested in {NICKNAME}'s cooking training!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what is this cooking training exactly...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It happened in the last Festival Utsava. Nara made lots of food for Aranara to try.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: So, to make food for Nara in return in this Festival Utsava, Arachatora and the others have been taking cooking training.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't wait any longer for this Festival Utsava!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Delicious food is the common language of all living creatures! It'll be fine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Arapacati, since you know where they are, why don't you search for them yourself?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: The magnificent Festival Utsava is about to begin. Arapacati has lots to prepare. No time to search for them.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: They left Vanarana for cooking training to prepare for Festival Utsava. But they don't know Festival Utsava is about to start! Arachatora, Arasaka, Arapas, and Araphala stupid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Then leave it to us! We'll be going with Arama to find the Aranara in the forest and prepare for Festival Utsava anyway. Isn't that right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how will we find Arachatora, Ara... What were the other names again?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Arachatora, Arasaka, Arapas, and Araphala.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh! Arana, Arama, Araja, Arapacati... Aranara names are so hard to remember!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Paimon, don't say that about Aranara names. You're gonna make the Aranara sad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, okay. So, how do we find them?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: They used to do cooking training in Vanarana. But they made lots of smoke, so Arapacati kicked them out.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Everyone was so scared then. Some Aranara even hibernated. Luckily, Arama was brave and punished the smoke. Arapacati was furious and made them leave.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: So, you should be able to find them in the forest by looking for <color=#00E1FFFF>the rising pillars of smoke</color>, I think.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you kicked them out!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Yes. Did I make a mistake?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, not really... Anyway, {NICKNAME}, let's get going!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Oh, right. One more thing. If my brothers are acting strange, go splat them with <color=#00E1FFFF>the power of Dendro</color>.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: In the past, they created lots and lots of smoke. Filled all of Vanarana with smoke. They were afraid too and ran around everywhere. Sometimes they also became like that if they touched strange mushrooms.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: But Aranara are spirits of the forest. So, we can recover and regain our senses by absorbing <color=#00E1FFFF>the power of Dendro</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon gets it now. By that logic, {NICKNAME} recovers after eating Sweet Madame, so {NICKNAME} must be a Sweet Madame spirit. Yes! This makes perfect sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Aaaanyway, let's go!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Good luck, Nara {NICKNAME}! Good luck, Paimon!

choices.text: I know what that feels like...

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} understands how I feel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, {NICKNAME} has a lost {F#brother}{M#sister} too...

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Oh. Nara {NICKNAME}, is your {F#brother}{M#sister} also doing cooking training?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Paimon thinks there's been a misunderstanding... Missing means you don't know where something has gone!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Oh, not that. Arapacati knows big brothers not missing. They go for training outside Vanarana for a long, long time. Cooking training.

choices.text: Did the winds bring the seeds of those stories...?

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: ...So difficult to talk to Nara, and they are so tall.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #Eek! It's Nara {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati not scared. Brothers are very brave, so they definitely not scared too.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: You should find them if you move towards <color=#00E1FFFF>the pillars of smoke</color>. If they are acting strange, go splat them with <color=#00E1FFFF>the power of Dendro</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati is sooo mad! Argh! More mad than mad!

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Forest is very dangerous as Marana is rampant there. When they left, Arapacati reminded brothers to work together...

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: But you started arguing right after leaving. Arachatora, you even ate strange thing.

dialogues.speaker: Arachatora
dialogues.text: *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati has decided. Arachatora not allowed to pick mushrooms until Sunsettias have ripened ten times.

dialogues.speaker: Arachatora
dialogues.text: Noooo... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Exactly! What would we do if he brought back bad spores and mushroom monsters grew here?

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Araphala, you too! You went so far away from Vanarana to collect fruits. There are many bad things over there! Araja told us about it especially!

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: That's right. Fruits need to drink water and Aranara need to drink water, so water is the best.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapas, of all places, you had to go to the Varuna Contraption. Don't you know that even Nara Varuna said the water of Vanarana is the most delicious?

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: Y—You see, only the "taste of happiness" can bring happiness to our little sister.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #Arasaka, I heard you caused a lot of trouble for Nara {NICKNAME} because of your "taste of happiness"...

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: E—Everything I did was for the "Supreme Delicacy"...

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: The purpose of making the "Supreme Delicacy" is to show the fruits of the "cooking training". Alas, what's the point of the training if you could only complete it with someone else's help?

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati thinks Arasaka needs to reflect on himself the most.

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arapacati! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} shared Arapacati's trouble with Paimon and solved the problem at its source...

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati no longer needs to worry about brothers missing Festival Utsava or being in danger outside. It's all thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Arapacati and brothers are all thankful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's something Paimon has always been curious about...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who is this Nara Varuna?

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #{F#He}{M#She} is our friend, a friend of Vanarana.

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #A friend of Aranara from a long, long time ago. A Golden Nara just like Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. But Paimon's still got another question for you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it about her brothers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes. Arapacati, which one of them is your biggest brother, and which one's the smallest?

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Hmm? The biggest and the smallest?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Ages... Ah, Arapacati understands. Just like tree rings. Hmm, the children of the forest aren't distinguished by age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Then why are they your brothers and why are you their younger sister?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Oh, this. We once had a Nara friend. Nara Varuna. {F#He}{M#She} said {F#he}{M#she} had a "{F#sister}{M#brother}."

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #When Arapacati and brothers listened to {F#him}{M#her} talk about the "{F#sister}{M#brother}," Nara Varuna looked happy and sad at the same time.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: That's how we understood. To an "older brother," a "younger sister" is an important Nara. To a "younger sister," an "older brother" is an important Nara.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: We thought it was great, so Arapacati and brothers decided to become brothers and sister. Nara Varuna said this was great. We should cherish our family.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's right, we must cherish our family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's one more thing Paimon's been wondering... Do Aranara need to eat?

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Humans cook ingredients into food, and the children of the forest can also make ingredients into food.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Nara Varuna taught us how Nara eat. That's why Arapacati and brothers started doing cooking training...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but that's certainly unusual...

choices.text: It's like you're playing a game...

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Arapacati and brothers are very serious because Nara Varuna said that to be able to share food is a very happy thing.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Oh and Arapas said that Nara {NICKNAME} knows how to cook too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah! {NICKNAME}'s cooking skills have been tested by time!

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: #Arapacati gets it... Nara {NICKNAME} must come to Festival Utsava and cook with Arapacati's bush-league brothers.

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Impress them once again with real cooking skills and food that only Nara can understand and Aranara will never understand.

choices.text: Try not to be surprised by then...

response.speaker: Arapacati
response.text: Arapacati is looking forward to it. This Festival Utsava will be really great and amazing!

choices.text: I'll show you what I've got!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! Paimon is asking about their ages!

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: #Thank you for everything, Nara {NICKNAME}. When the time comes for Festival Utsava, you must come as well!

dialogues.speaker: Arachatora
dialogues.text: I can't pick any mushrooms until the Sunsettias have ripened ten times. *sob* I know it's not a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Arachatora
dialogues.text: But for some reason, just thinking about it slows time to a crawl...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Arapacati is so scary when she's angry. I hope she won't be so angry after she has had some fruit...

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Vanarana's water is good, but it's water that's right within reach... But we can try using that water to cook next time!

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: The "taste of happiness" doesn't bring happiness but bitterness instead? How can this be?
